introduction: On this Sunday, God tells Israel at Sinai that they will be his treasured possession, a kingdom of priests and a holy nation. In the Gospel, Jesus is moved with compassion for the crowds, like sheep without a shepherd; he asks us to pray for laborers for the harvest and sends out the Twelve. Paul tells us that God proves his love for us in that Christ died for us while we were still sinners. Let us go out with the compassion of Christ.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the harvest is abundant but the laborers are few. Let us pray to the Lord of the harvest.
intentions: For the Church: that she may look on the crowds with the compassion of Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For vocations to the priesthood and religious life: that the Lord of the harvest may send many laborers. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the sick and all who are troubled and abandoned: that Christ's disciples may bring them healing and care. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are lost and without direction: that they may find the Good Shepherd. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that, having received freely, we may give freely. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, your Son was moved with compassion for the crowds. Send laborers into your harvest, and make us generous messengers of your love. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Freely you have received
reflection.body:
At Mount Sinai, God reminds Israel of what he has done: "You have seen what I did to the Egyptians, and how I bore you on eagles' wings, and brought you to myself." Then he gives them their calling: "you shall be to me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation." They are chosen not for privilege but for service, to bring God to the world.

In the Gospel, Jesus looks at the crowds, and "he was moved with compassion for them because they were harassed and scattered, like sheep without a shepherd." His response begins with prayer: "The harvest indeed is plentiful, but the laborers are few. Pray therefore that the Lord of the harvest will send out laborers into his harvest."

Then he becomes the answer to his own prayer. He calls the twelve apostles by name, from Simon Peter to Judas Iscariot, and sends them out with authority to heal and to proclaim the Kingdom. He gives them one guiding principle: "Freely you received, so freely give."

Everything we have from God is a gift. The faith we received, the love we have known, the forgiveness we have been given: all of it is meant to be passed on.

Paul tells us how freely we have received: "while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us." God did not wait for us to deserve his love. "For if while we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we will be saved by his life."

This week, pray each day for laborers for the harvest: for priests, religious and lay people who serve. Look at the people around you with the compassion of Jesus. And give freely what you have freely received: your time, your faith, your care.
